images.title: Cutting 2856 into two easy parts
images.purpose: Show 2856 cut into 2800 and 56 and each part divided by 7.
images.composition: One long bar cut into a big part and a small part, with an arrow from each part to its quotient.
images.exact_structure: Plain white frame, 1456 by 816. One bar made of two rectangles joined end to end, 100 px high, at y 200 to 300 (the bar is not drawn to scale). The left rectangle is teal #0072B2, x 128 to 1088, with the white label 2800 centred in it (56 px). The right rectangle is amber #E69F00, x 1088 to 1328, with the dark label 56 centred in it (56 px). Both have a thin dark #2B2B2B outline. Above the bar, a grey #6B7280 bracket (4 px) spans x 128 to 1328 at y 170 with the label 2856 centred above it at x 728 and y 125 (56 px, dark). Under the bar two grey arrows (4 px, 120 px long) point straight down: one from x 608, y 300 to y 420 and one from x 1208, y 300 to y 420, each with the label ÷ 7 (44 px, dark) 20 px to its right. Under the arrows two rounded rectangles with thin dark outlines and white fill, 200 px wide and 100 px high, at y 420 to 520: the left one at x 508 to 708 holds 400 and the right one at x 1108 to 1308 holds 8 (56 px, dark). Nothing else in the frame.

images.takeaway: A hard division can be done by cutting the number into parts the divisor divides easily.
images.description: A bar for 2856 cut into 2800 and 56, each part divided by 7 giving 400 and 8.
images.context: Concept image for Split the Number into Convenient Parts. The numbers are the plan's own worked example, not a number of any book question.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student why 7 divides 2800 and 56 easily. The slip to watch: cutting the number where the parts are not easy to divide.

image_decisions.why: The cut bar with its two quotients is the mathematics of splitting a number into convenient parts.
